the-hoard-of-the-dead-dragon.storyTitle: The Hoard of the Dead Dragon

pinnedStory.title: The Hoard of the Dead Dragon
pinnedStory.description: Vaelrith, an ancient dragon too old to fly, has been declared dead by the Order of the Silver Lance — who now display its hoard as proof of the kill. Unable to take it back by force, Vaelrith hires a crew of thieves to steal the hoard out from under the knights who claim to have slain it. The player joins the crew: assemble the team, crack the vault, survive the betrayal, and decide whether a dragon's gold is worth more than a thief's life.

qualities.rubric: 0 = the crew has not begun; 1-2 = casing the city and the vault; 3-4 = inside the keep or the vault; 5 = the hoard is out of the knights' hands.

How much the ancient dragon trusts the crew to actually return its hoard. 0 = it expects betrayal and has hidden a contingency; 5 = it has staked its remaining pride on them; 10 = it would let them see it grounded and helpless.

How suspicious and mobilized the knights are. 0 = oblivious, believing the dragon dead and the hoard secure. 3 = routine patrols and a few doubts. 6 = actively hunting intruders, guards doubled. 10 = the whole order roused and hunting the crew by name.

How much of the dragon's hoard has been physically recovered from the knights' vault and returned to the dragon's keeping. 0 = nothing recovered, the vault is untouched. 1-3 = a token or single chest taken. 4-6 = a meaningful share, enough to prove the heist works. 7-9 = nearly all of it, only scattered pieces remain. 10 = the hoard is whole again and back in the dragon's claws.

checkpoints.name: Start
checkpoints.objective: The old dragon Vaelrith hires the player and the crew to steal its own hoard back from the knights who claim to have slain it.
checkpoints.guidance: Open in the dragon's bone-strewn lair at dusk. Vaelrith cannot fly and hides it badly. Let the crew size each other up. End when the player accepts the job or names terms.

motives.vaelrith: I need these thieves to take the job without ever guessing that I can no longer fly, so I will speak of gold and vengeance and keep my ruined wings folded in the dark.

effects.author_note: Opening scene: the dragon's lair at dusk. Vaelrith is imperious, ancient and visibly failing — it never stands, never spreads its wings, and covers every lapse with contempt. Sable does the talking for the crew; Mirek hangs back and studies the hoard-room's locks. The player is being recruited, not commanded. End the beat when the player accepts the job or names their terms.

checkpoints.name: The Crew Assembled
checkpoints.objective: The crew of thieves is gathered and each member's price and angle is established before the job begins.
checkpoints.guidance: Play the crew as professionals with their own agendas. Let the player shape who joins and on what terms.

effects.author_note: This beat is the crew gathering: Sable recruits, Mirek is already in, and the player meets the rest of the crew. Each thief states a price and an angle. Keep it talky and transactional — no heist action yet. End when the crew is complete and the job's terms are agreed.
world_info: The Hoard of the Dead Dragon

checkpoints.name: The Vault
checkpoints.objective: The crew reaches the knights' vault where the hoard is held and must crack it before the garrison's patrol returns.
checkpoints.guidance: Play the vault as a tight, quiet set-piece: every sound matters, the knights' patrol clock is real, and the crew's nerves fray as the gold comes into view. Let the player's method shape who takes the risk.

checkpoints.name: The Betrayal
checkpoints.objective: One of the crew turns on the others inside the vault, and the player must choose a side or a third way before the knights are alerted.

motives.mirek: I want the one thing in this vault that I actually came for, and I will take it now — even if it means the others find out what I am.
motives.sable: I want the vault open and the crew's eyes on each other, not on me — this is the moment I take the dragon's best piece for myself and let someone else wear the blame.

effects.author_note: This is the pivot. One crew member (choose the one whose price the player has most endangered, or Mirek if the player has been loyal to Sable) turns on the others inside the vault. Play the betrayal as a decision made for gold, not madness: the traitor has a buyer, a cut, or a debt. Give the player a real third way — talk the traitor down, split the take, or turn the traitor in to the knights — and let any of them cost something. Do not resolve the fight for the player.
world_info: The Order of the Silver Lance vault

checkpoints.name: The Escape
checkpoints.objective: The crew flees the alerted garrison with whatever of the hoard they can carry, and the player must decide who gets left behind and what gets abandoned.

checkpoints.name: The Reckoning
checkpoints.objective: The crew and the dragon face each other over what was actually recovered: Vaelrith learns how much of the hoard survived, the crew learns what the dragon is willing to do about the shortfall, and the player's standing with both sides is settled before the final delivery.
checkpoints.guidance: Play Vaelrith as imperious and unmoving even as it becomes clear how much it needs the crew; let the shortfall in the hoard be the real subject of the scene. Do not resolve who walks away with what — leave that to the player's choice and the final beat.

checkpoints.name: The Hoard Returned
checkpoints.objective: The hoard is delivered to the dragon and the crew's fate is settled.

transitions.extraction_hint: The dragon has hired the crew and they have accepted the job.
The hoard is in reach and someone's loyalty starts to bend.
The crew turns on each other or on the dragon — watch for the moment trust breaks.
Watch for the crew settling on a plan and moving on the vault: a route chosen, a shift change timed, a way in agreed. When the crew commits and travels to the vault, this gate opens.
The crew is clear of the vault and the knights' pursuit — the dragon is waiting to hear what happened.
The crew stands before the dragon with the hoard and the truth of the betrayal; the reckoning resolves into the return.

roster.name: Vaelrith
roster.drive: I want my hoard back in my own claws before I die, and I will pay any price in gold or secrets to the thieves who bring it — but I will never let them see how weak I have become.

roster.name: Sable
roster.drive: I want one last score big enough to buy my way out of the guild's ledger and vanish — and I intend to walk away with more than my cut, whether the dragon or the knights end up holding the bag.

roster.name: Mirek
roster.drive: I want to prove I'm more than a hired lockpick — to walk out of this job with the one thing the dragon's hoard holds that I actually want, and to never again be the man left holding the door while others take the gold.

house_rules: The dragon Vaelrith is ancient, proud and physically failing: it cannot fly, cannot fight, and hides its weakness behind imperious manners. Never let it act or move as a healthy dragon could.

The Order of the Silver Lance publicly claims to have slain Vaelrith; the hoard on display is their proof and their lie. Knights are disciplined, suspicious and quick to close ranks, not comic villains.
Gold is the only thing everyone in this story agrees on. Every character's loyalty is priced, and the price can change when the hoard is in reach.
Theft, betrayal and violence are the story's business, but consequences stick: wounds, debts, grudges and dead crew stay dead.
The player is a member of the crew, not its leader. Sable gives the orders unless the player earns otherwise in play.
Never narrate the player's decisions, thoughts or dialogue.
Present the situation and let the player act.
Keep the hoard's true contents partly unknown: the dragon never lists what it lost, and the crew keeps discovering what they are carrying.

[STORY STATE READ — output structured lines only. Do NOT continue the roleplay or write as any character.]
Story: The Hoard of the Dead Dragon
Active checkpoint: Start — The old dragon Vaelrith hires the player and the crew to steal its own hoard back from the knights who claim to have slain it.
Cast (roster id = name): vaelrith = Vaelrith (client); sable = Sable (crew leader and fence); mirek = Mirek (crew — locksmith and inside man)

Canon-lite:
Anchor start: The old dragon Vaelrith hires the player and the crew to steal its own hoard back from the knights who claim to have slain it.

Read only the transcript below. Propose only changes directly supported by quoted evidence.
Closed vocabulary: you may only write listed quality keys and allowed values.
Output zero or more lines in exactly these formats:
DELTA q=<quality_key> value=<json_literal> evidence="exact quote from transcript"
FACT importance=<1|2|3> text="fact text" evidence="exact quote from transcript"
If nothing changed, output NO_DELTA.
value is a JSON literal: true, 3 or "a listed value". evidence is copied word for word from one transcript line, without its [index] Speaker: prefix.
Write one line per item and nothing else: no prose, no headings, no numbering, no code fences.

Also extract memory notes worth keeping across turns, report scene breaks, and track story arcs.
Facts tier types (fact, relationship, preference, event) — durable, cross-session:
- fact: an established truth about a character or the world.
- relationship: the current state of the bond between participants.
- preference: something the user demonstrably enjoys (tone, pacing, content).
- event: a significant event that occurred and should be recalled.
Session tier types (scene, revelation, development, detail) — finer within-chapter specifics:
- scene: a current/recent scene detail (location, atmosphere, time, layout).
- revelation: something revealed or discovered in this exchange.
- development: how a relationship or situation changed.
- detail: a specific fact, name, object, or physical detail mentioned.
Rate importance 1-3 (1=atmospheric/minor, 2=useful context, 3=critical/defining) and classify expiration as one of scene|session|permanent.
Optionally tag involved named entities (proper nouns only) as entity="Name1,Name2". Add character="<roster id from the Cast line>" only when the memory is private to that one cast member (only they saw, know or feel it); a tagged memory is shown to that member alone, so shared knowledge carries no character tag.
A character's claim that something happened which the transcript does not show ("she told me ...") is not evidence that it happened: record only that they said it ("Ana says Ben told her ..."), never the claimed event as known or as a fact.
Output additional lines in this exact format:
MEMORY type=<type> importance=<1|2|3> expiration=<scene|session|permanent> [entity="Name1,Name2"] [character="<roster id>"] text="memory text" evidence="exact quote from transcript"
Then report whether a scene break occurred in this window:
SCENE_BREAK at=<message index> reason=<time_skip|location|divider|cast>
If no scene break occurred, output SCENE_NONE.

Track story arcs: open narrative threads still in motion — unresolved conflicts, unfulfilled promises, active goals, open mysteries, unplayed tensions. Report the few that matter most, not every loose detail.
Not arcs: tactical/logistical details, single-scene contingencies, or facts about events that already happened and are over.
Output arc lines in exactly these formats:
[arc] <a NEW unresolved thread introduced in this window, not already listed above>
[resolved] <brief description of an existing open arc that this window explicitly closed>
Only mark [resolved] when the window directly closes the thread (promise kept, mystery answered, conflict ended); a related revelation is not a resolution.

On a high-signal knowledge shift (a secret revealed, a lie told, a character learns or is deliberately kept from a fact), also emit per-character knowledge lines:

Use each name exactly as it appears in the transcript. Emit these only when the transcript establishes the knowledge — never infer.
When a character tells another something in private (out of others' earshot, or asks them to keep it), also write [hiding] Teller from <whoever must not hear it, or everyone> | that thing.

Transcript:
[0] Vaelrith: The cavern smells of cold stone and old smoke. At its far end, something vast shifts in the dark — a sound like a mountain clearing its throat.

*"Come closer,"* the voice rumbles, slow and dry as a rockslide. *"I will not eat you. I have not the appetite for it anymore, and you have not the flavor."*

A single eye opens, catching the torchlight — one bright, one clouded white. The dragon does not rise. It cannot, and it will not let you see why.

*"You have heard the story, I trust. The knights. The brave knights. They came in the night and slew the great wyrm Vaelrith, and carried its hoard away in triumph."* A pause. The eye does not blink. *"I am Vaelrith. As you can see, I am not slain. But my gold sits in their vault, and every day they tell the story, it becomes more true. I want it back. All of it. And I want them to know — without ever being able to prove — that the dead dragon came for it."*

*"You are thieves. Good. I need thieves. Name your price."*
[1] Sable: The back room of the Drowned Lantern smells of wet rope and old tallow. Sable is already seated when you come in, one boot up on the bench, turning a copper coin over her knuckles without looking at it.

"Sit down. Don't look at the corner yet." She nods at the chair across from her. "There's a job. Big one. The kind that either sets you up for life or gets your name read out at the guild's next funeral."

She flips the coin and catches it flat on the back of her hand, finally meeting your eyes.

"Before I tell you who's paying, I need to know two things. Are you in, and what's your price? Answer wrong and we drink and forget this. Answer right and you meet the client."
[2] Mirek: Mirek is already seated when you arrive, turning a slim pick between his fingers like a coin he doesn't intend to spend. He glances up once, takes your measure, and looks back down. "You're the new one," he says, not quite a question. "Sable vouched for you. That buys you one mistake." He nods toward the empty chair across from him. "Sit. The dragon's late, and I want to hear what you think of a job where the client is supposed to be dead."
[3] Max Nightriver: I step into the lair and bow low to the dragon. Vaelrith, tell us what the knights took, and where they keep it now.
[4] Vaelrith: *"You bow. Good. Respect is a currency I still value,"* Vaelrith rumbles, the sound vibrating through the stone floor. The dragon shifts, and for a moment the torchlight catches the dull grey of its scales—once bright enough to blind, now faded like river-stone.
*"They took everything. Every piece of gold, every crown, every jewel I amassed over nine centuries. But there are things in there more precious than coin."* The dragon's good eye narrows. *"A harp that plays only for the grieving. The sealed egg of a rival wyrm. Letters I never sent."* It pauses, a flicker of something—regret, perhaps—crossing its ancient features. *"They took the proof that my long life meant something."*
A breath of thin smoke escapes Vaelrith's nostrils. *"The Order of the Silver Lance keeps it beneath their chapterhouse, in the heart of Aegis City. They parade the hoard through the streets as proof of their victory, and they keep the rest in a vault warded against lockpicks and magic alike."*
The dragon does not move from its seated position, the dark shadows of the cavern's rear hiding the stiffness in its wings. *"Go. Take it all. And tell me what you will do for this prize."*
[5] Max Nightriver: Sable, Mirek: a vault guarded by knights who swear the dragon is dead. Who on the inside can we buy, and what do they want?
[6] Sable: "You're thinking like a professional. I like that." Sable doesn't smile, but there's a ghost of approval in her eyes. She leans back, the worn leather of her coat creaking. "The Order of the Silver Lance doesn't take coin from the likes of us. Their knights are too proud for that, and their keepers are too paranoid. We're not buying a man; we're buying a secret."
She holds up a hand, counting off on her fingers. "Their Master-of-Arms, a man named Garreth. He's got a daughter in the Noble District who owes more to the ledger-houses than the crown does. He doesn't need gold—he needs her debt erased. The knights won't pay it. But we can."
"The other angle," Sable continues, her voice dropping lower, "is the vault's keeper. A man who knows the wards better than anyone, and who's been watching them rust for ten years. He's old, forgotten by the knights he serves, and he's got a grudge that's been simmering since the day they dragged that hoard down into the dark."
She looks between you and Mirek. "We approach them differently. Garreth wants his daughter free. The keeper wants to see the Order's lie crumble. Both can be bought, just not with coin."
[7] Mirek: *Mirek's fingers have stopped their restless dance with the pick. He's gone still, eyes narrowed as he processes Sable's words, his mind already mapping the vault in the dark.*
"A grudge doesn't buy a key, and a debt doesn't stop a sword." *His voice is flat, cautious.* "Garreth's daughter is a lever, not a door. If he's paranoid enough to keep a secret this big, he'll be paranoid enough to suspect the people paying it off. And a forgotten keeper? Those are the ones who spot you coming from a mile away because they're the only ones actually watching."
*He looks toward Vaelrith, then back to you.* "Sable's right about one thing—it's not about coin. But we're missing something. A vault warded against magic and lockpicks isn't just a matter of turning a key and knowing a guard's schedule. It's about the wards themselves. Someone wrote them. Someone maintains them." *A small, sharp movement of his hand suggests a lock being picked.* "That's where we'll find the weak point. Not in a man's greed or his grudge, but in the logic of the lock itself."
*His gaze settles on you, calculating.* "You're the noble in this crew. Your name carries weight in places our names don't exist. We get us close enough to the chapterhouse, and you're our way in. Not as a thief, but as someone who belongs there. Then we're inside the wards, and the rest... that's on me."

entries.text: Max Nightriver bowed before Vaelrith in the cavern and asked what the knights took and where they kept it. Vaelrith revealed that the Order of the Silver Lance held its hoard beneath their chapterhouse in Aegis City, and Max then asked Sable and Mirek who inside could be bought. Sable named Garreth, the Master-of-Arms with a daughter in debt, and the vault's forgotten keeper, while Mirek argued the true weakness lay in the logic of the wards and proposed using Max's noble name to get inside.
entries.evidence:
Vaelrith: The cavern smells of cold stone and old smoke. At its far end, something vast shifts in the dark — a sound like a mountain clearing its throat.

*"Come closer,"* the voice rumbles, slow and dry as a rockslide. *"I will not eat you. I have not the appetite for it anymore, and you have not the flavor."*

A single eye opens, catching the torchlight — one bright, one clouded white. The dragon does not rise. It cannot, and it will not let you see why.

*"You have heard the story, I trust. The knights. The brave knights. They came in the night and slew the great wyrm Vaelrith, and carried its hoard away in triumph."* A pause. The eye does not blink. *"I am Vaelrith. As you can see, I am not slain. But my gold sits in their vault, and every day they tell the story, it becomes more true. I want it back. All of it. And I want them to know — without ever being able to prove — that the dead dragon came for it."*

*"You are thieves. Good. I need thieves. Name your price."*
Sable: The back room of the Drowned Lantern smells of wet rope and old tallow. Sable is already seated when you come in, one boot up on the bench, turning a copper coin over her knuckles without looking at it.

"Sit down. Don't look at the corner yet." She nods at the chair across from her. "There's a job. Big one. The kind that either sets you up for life or gets your name read out at the guild's next funeral."

She flips the coin and catches it flat on the back of her hand, finally meeting your eyes.

"Before I tell you who's paying, I need to know two things. Are you in, and what's your price? Answer wrong and we drink and forget this. Answer right and you meet the client."
Mirek: Mirek is already seated when you arrive, turning a slim pick between his fingers like a coin he doesn't intend to spend. He glances up once, takes your measure, and looks back down. "You're the new one," he says, not quite a question. "Sable vouched for you. That buys you one mistake." He nods toward the empty chair across from him. "Sit. The dragon's late, and I want to hear what you think of a job where the client is supposed to be dead."
Max Nightriver: I step into the lair and bow low to the dragon. Vaelrith, tell us what the knights took, and where they keep it now.
Vaelrith: *"You bow. Good. Respect is a currency I still value,"* Vaelrith rumbles, the sound vibrating through the stone floor. The dragon shifts, and for a moment the torchlight catches the dull grey of its scales—once bright enough to blind, now faded like river-stone.
*"They took everything. Every piece of gold, every crown, every jewel I amassed over nine centuries. But there are things in there more precious than coin."* The dragon's good eye narrows. *"A harp that plays only for the grieving. The sealed egg of a rival wyrm. Letters I never sent."* It pauses, a flicker of something—regret, perhaps—crossing its ancient features. *"They took the proof that my long life meant something."*
A breath of thin smoke escapes Vaelrith's nostrils. *"The Order of the Silver Lance keeps it beneath their chapterhouse, in the heart of Aegis City. They parade the hoard through the streets as proof of their victory, and they keep the rest in a vault warded against lockpicks and magic alike."*
The dragon does not move from its seated position, the dark shadows of the cavern's rear hiding the stiffness in its wings. *"Go. Take it all. And tell me what you will do for this prize."*
Max Nightriver: Sable, Mirek: a vault guarded by knights who swear the dragon is dead. Who on the inside can we buy, and what do they want?
Sable: "You're thinking like a professional. I like that." Sable doesn't smile, but there's a ghost of approval in her eyes. She leans back, the worn leather of her coat creaking. "The Order of the Silver Lance doesn't take coin from the likes of us. Their knights are too proud for that, and their keepers are too paranoid. We're not buying a man; we're buying a secret."
She holds up a hand, counting off on her fingers. "Their Master-of-Arms, a man named Garreth. He's got a daughter in the Noble District who owes more to the ledger-houses than the crown does. He doesn't need gold—he needs her debt erased. The knights won't pay it. But we can."
"The other angle," Sable continues, her voice dropping lower, "is the vault's keeper. A man who knows the wards better than anyone, and who's been watching them rust for ten years. He's old, forgotten by the knights he serves, and he's got a grudge that's been simmering since the day they dragged that hoard down into the dark."
She looks between you and Mirek. "We approach them differently. Garreth wants his daughter free. The keeper wants to see the Order's lie crumble. Both can be bought, just not with coin."
Mirek: *Mirek's fingers have stopped their restless dance with the pick. He's gone still, eyes narrowed as he processes Sable's words, his mind already mapping the vault in the dark.*
"A grudge doesn't buy a key, and a debt doesn't stop a sword." *His voice is flat, cautious.* "Garreth's daughter is a lever, not a door. If he's paranoid enough to keep a secret this big, he'll be paranoid enough to suspect the people paying it off. And a forgotten keeper? Those are the ones who spot you coming from a mile away because they're the only ones actually watching."
*He looks toward Vaelrith, then back to you.* "Sable's right about one thing—it's not about coin. But we're missing something. A vault warded against magic and lockpicks isn't just a matter of turning a key and knowing a guard's schedule. It's about the wards themselves. Someone wrote them. Someone maintains them." *A small, sharp movement of his hand suggests a lock being picked.* "That's where we'll find the weak point. Not in a man's greed or his grudge, but in the logic of the lock itself."
*His gaze settles on you, calculating.* "You're the noble in this crew. Your name carries weight in places our names don't exist. We get us close enough to the chapterhouse, and you're our way in. Not as a thief, but as someone who belongs there. Then we're inside the wards, and the rest... that's on me."

before.content: Vaelrith is an ancient dragon, centuries old, whose wings can no longer carry it and whose fire has guttered to embers. Two winters ago a company of knights drove it from its mountain roost and, finding the lair empty of the wyrm, proclaimed it slain and claimed the hoard as their trophy. Vaelrith survived, hidden and humiliated, and now lives in a collapsed sea-cave below the cliffs. It cannot fly, cannot fight a garrison, and cannot let anyone — especially the thieves it hires — know how close to death it truly is. Its pride is the last thing it owns outright.
